title: ork wait: block until a run changes state
lead: *Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-09 at HEAD 4707be4. Size M recommended. Status: READY once the exit-code numbers and the state list are answered (Q1, Q2). Owner already decided the shape on 2026-11-07 (distinct exit codes for question pending, state changed, nothing active and timeout; `--json` prints the new state). Share the state list and codes with S311 and S312.
findings_note: Wave 6, 2026-11-02: an agent or script that steers ork from the CLI has no way to wait for a change. The orchestrator session polls ork status in a shell loop (.scratch/v11/watch.sh, zsh-only) and restarts it each time it fires. Proposed: 'ork wait [RUN] [--timeout D]' prints the status block and exits when a run's state, item or step changes, a question is pending, or no run is active; exit code says which. The daemon already pushes snapshots to the TUI, so the CLI can reuse them. Owner decision needed on the exit codes and on --json. Related: S237 (answer and retry return at once), S233 (ork ai guide), S240 (status text clarity).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- Owner evidence 2026-11-04: `.scratch/v11/watch.sh` exits on any status change, including every output tick of a running role; it fired about ten times for one slice. Wanted: `ork wait RUN --until awaiting-approval,paused,stopped,landed` that blocks until the run enters one of those states and prints the state.
- Wave 6, 2026-11-02 (S257 findings): the orchestrator polls `ork status` in a shell loop and restarts it each time.
- Waves 7-8, 2026-11-03 to 11-05 (friction F50, F55): runs watched with until-loops over `ork status`; approve output was nohup'd to a log and grepped for "committed"; `ork retry` was refused as busy while the run's reviewer still ran.
- Code at HEAD: the commands are dispatched in `Run` (`internal/cli/cli.go:262-306`); exit codes are 0, 1, 2 only (`cli.go:23-27`, help text `cli.go:166`). `ork show RUN` reads `daemon.ShowReply` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2041`: `State`, `Reason`, `Next`, `Pending.Kind`) through `MethodRunShow` (`internal/cli/show.go:34`). The daemon pushes `SnapshotChanged` notices to a subscribed connection (`internal/daemon/subscribe.go:73`, `client.go:146`, `:155`), but a notice only names a project and parts. So a wait subscribes, then re-reads `run.show` on each notice. Whether every run state change sends a notice was not verified; the spec adds a periodic re-read as a safety net.
- States: `runrec` has `awaiting-approval`, `paused`, `stopped`, `committed`, `queued` (`internal/runrec/record.go:20-34`). A question pause is `paused` with `Pending.Kind == "question"` (`record.go:157`). "landed" is `committed` with `LandedAt` set (`record.go:320`); "failed" is not a record state (see Q2).
- Overlap: S311 (notify command, filed 2026-11-09) is the push side and shares the state list and exit codes; S312 refers to `ork wait`'s exit codes. S265 (busy rule for retry) is separate and not in this slice. Slicer has no wait command (`slicer --root ../slicer find wait` finds only unrelated items).

### Open questions

1. Exit code numbers. Options: (a) 0 changed to an until state, 3 question pending, 4 nothing active, 5 timeout (recommended: keeps 1 failure and 2 usage, and codes sit above 2); (b) 0 for state changed, question pending, nothing active and timeout each separate, with timeout 124 as `timeout(1)` does; (c) 10-13. Key: `cli.wait-exit-codes`.
2. The state list shared with S311. Options: (a) `question`, `awaiting-approval`, `paused`, `stopped`, `landed`, `failed`, where `failed` means a ledger run that ended with outcome fail (needs a read of the ledger, unverified) (recommended: the list S311 already names); (b) drop `failed` until a record state exists; (c) use raw record states only. Key: `cli.run-event-states`.
3. With no RUN argument, what does wait follow? Options: (a) the project's single unfinished run, an error if there are several (recommended); (b) any run of the project; (c) require RUN. Key: `cli.wait-default-run`.

sections.body:

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/cli/wait_test.go`, with a fake daemon on a real socket that serves `run.show` replies and `snapshot.changed` notices (`waitFake`; the `App.Call` double of `show_test.go` cannot carry notices). Exit codes (adj 201): 0 changed to an until state or any change without `--until`, 3 question pending, 4 nothing active, 5 timeout. The state list has no `failed` (adj 247, `cli.wait-failed-state`).

- `TestWaitReturnsWhenTheRunEntersAnUntilState`: replies implement, implement, `awaiting-approval`. Assert exit 0 and stdout `r1 awaiting-approval`; assert three reads and one connection.
- `TestWaitIgnoresOutputTicks`: ten notices with state `implement` unchanged; assert it keeps waiting, then returns on `paused`.
- `TestWaitQuestionPendingHasItsOwnExitCode`: `paused` with pending kind `question`; assert exit 3 and stdout names the decision key and the next command.
- `TestWaitStateChangedExitCode`: no `--until`; any change of state returns exit 0 with the new state.
- `TestWaitNothingActive`: a final run, an unknown run, a final run that never entered the until list, and no unfinished run in the project; assert exit 4 and a one-line stderr message.
- `TestWaitTimeout`: `--timeout 50ms` with no change; assert exit 5.
- `TestWaitJSONPrintsTheNewState`: `--json` prints `{"run","item","state","reason","next","pending":{"kind"}}`; assert the fields and that stdout holds only the JSON. `TestWaitJSONFailureIsAnErrorObject`: a timeout prints the error object.
- `TestWaitUntilRejectsAnUnknownState`: usage error, exit 2, lists the valid states (also for `failed`). `TestWaitHasNoFailedState`: `RunEventStates` is question, awaiting-approval, paused, stopped, landed; `--until failed` is an unknown state and the valid list does not offer it.
- `TestWaitAlreadyInAnUntilStateReturnsAtOnce`: the first read is already in the list; one read.
- `TestWaitReadsAgainWhenNoNoticeComes`: the poll reads again without a notice.
- `TestWaitReconnectsAfterADaemonRestart`: the daemon ends twice; assert one daemon start per drop and no false exit.
- `TestWaitSubscribesToTheRegisteredProjects`, `TestWaitLandedIsACommittedRunThatLanded`, `TestWaitWithoutRunFollowsTheOnlyUnfinishedRun`, `TestWaitWithoutRunNeedsOneRunAndOneProject` (owner decision `cli.wait-project-scope`: `--project`), `TestWaitTakesRunAndFlags`.
- `TestExitCodesAreDistinct`: the four wait codes (0, 3, 4, 5) differ from each other, and 3, 4 and 5 differ from 1 and 2.

In `internal/daemon/show_test.go`: `TestRunShowSaysWhenARunLanded`: `run.show` has `landed` only for a committed run with `landed_at` set.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add `ork wait [RUN] [--until STATE,...] [--timeout D] [--json]` in `internal/cli/wait.go`. With no RUN it follows the project's newest unfinished run (name the rule in docs; see Q3).
2. Subscribe, read `run.show` at once, then on each notice and every 30 seconds, until a stop condition holds. Print `RUN STATE` plus `next:` for a pause, like `ork show`.
3. Return the codes from Q1. Keep 0, 1 and 2 as they are.
4. Do not change `ork status`, `ork show` or the retry busy rule. Do not add the notify command (S311).
5. Docs and CHANGELOG, marked *proposed*.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09, accepted the recommended answers): Exit code numbers -> (a) 0 changed to an until state, 3 question pending, 4 nothing active, 5 timeout (recommended: keeps 1 failure and 2 usage, and codes sit above 2) [cli.wait-exit-codes, adj 201]. The state list shared with S311 -> (a) `question`, `awaiting-approval`, `paused`, `stopped`, `landed`, `failed`, where `failed` means a ledger run that ended with outcome fail (needs a read of the ledger, unverified) (recommended: the list S311 already names) [cli.run-event-states, adj 202]. With no RUN argument, what does wait follow? -> (a) the project's single unfinished run, an error if there are several (recommended) [cli.wait-default-run, adj 203].

Owner decision (2026-11-09, interactive question): cli.wait-failed-state = drop failed from wait state list for now; S311 can add it when a record state exists.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09): How does `ork wait` with no RUN pick the project whose unfinished run it follows? -> --project flag: add `--project NAME` as `ork status` has it; with no RUN and no `--project`, use the only registered project, else a usage error [cli.wait-project-scope].
